description.narrative:
Rivers and Rights Foundation (R<(>&<)>R) is formerly International Rivers (IR) has partnership with Oxfam over ten years. Now, the Southeast Asia Team has separately as R<(>&<)>R registered as Thai Foundation and official recognized by authority from 1 October 2025 onward. R<(>&<)>R will be focusing on the following strategies.
We have a proven and evolving strategy that fosters grassroots connections, catalyses media campaigns, undertakes institutional research and analysis, and supports advocacy, and campaigns for greater inclusion of communities and marginalised groups in planning and decision-making. We combine an environmental and human rights approach and emphasize the importance of strengthening civil society and people’s movements.
Thematically, R<(>&<)>R, partners and allies will focus on the following key water governance policies, plans and projects:
• Large-scale transboundary hydropower projects, especially Mekong and Salween mainstream dams. For Salween mainstream dams, we will mainly play a monitoring role, given our analysis to date indicates that Salween mainstream dams are unlikely to progress significantly over the next three years due to ongoing conflict in Myanmar. For Mekong mainstream dams, we will focus on dams that are currently, or plan to export electricity to Thailand, as these also involve Thai developers and financiers and are also linked to the Thai Power Development Plan, which at time of writing has not yet been approved. Approaches and interventions will vary according to status of dams e.g. o Existing i.e. Xayaburi dam, where we’ll continue to advocate for greater transparency and disclosure, to counter narratives of sustainable hydropower. o Dams that have completed PNPCA process and signed Power Purchase Agreements with EGAT i.e.Pak Beng, Luang Prabang and Pak Lay dams, wherewe’ll continue to engage Thai actors and MRC (re Joint Action Plans), to raise critical concerns and questions, including noting how they are not needed for Thailand’s energy security. Given its location asthe most upper Lower Mekong mainstream dam, special attention will be given to Pak Beng dam regarding potential transboundary and cumulative impacts linked to transboundary water contamination/pollution from upstream mining. o Planned dams e.g. Sanakham, which still has not completed the PNPCA process and Phou Ngoy, which is next in line to undertake PNPCA, where the focus will be to stop/cancel the dams by targeting Thai government and financiers. • Transboundary river contamination in the Mekong and Salween basins o In the Mekong, build networks and advocate MRC and Development Partners to take more meaningful actions to go address the transboundary river pollution, including with reference to MRC strategic plan, 2026-2030, and using the opportunity of the MRC Summit in 2026 to elevate this issue. This will be complemented by regular engagement and advocacy to Thai government and related agencies to recognise - and develop actions in response to – community and civil society concerns o In the Salween initial focus will be on building community and civil society awareness and networks, including through community action research (e.g. CESD CMU in Tha Ta Fang), collaborations with academics and technical experts and government departments (such as PCD) to build evidence base, using media and campaigns to increase public pressure on Thai government and related agencies to take actions to address community concerns. o Building networks, including between Mekong and Salween basins, as well as at regional and international levels, given other existing networks working on critical minerals in Asia and beyond. • Proposed Large-scale water diversion projects in Thailand e.g. Yuam-Salween Water Diversion, Khon-Loe-Chi-Mun (KLCM) Water Diversion, bothof which have potential transboundary impacts on the Salween and Mekong rivers, respectively o While Yuam-Salween Water Diversion is currently suspended, in part due to our and partner advocacy under IP2 and beyond, given scale of impacts, it is important tocontinue to monitor and advocate on this project, with our aim being to cancel/stop the project. This will be done by e.g. scaling out People’s EIA to another affected community in Omkoi district (CESD), continuing to monitor and engage Thai government, andimportantly continue to engage and strengthen community networks and CSO and academic collaborations. o Similarly, status of KLCM scheme remainsuncertain, but it’s important to keep monitoring government policies and plans, as well as ensuring communitynetworks remain activeand strong in case project has a renewed push from the Thai government.
• Cross-cutting, advocating for greater transparency and accountability in cross-border investments, including alignment with UN Guiding Principles (UNGP) onBusiness and Human Rights (BHR) and other international guidelines and standards. o Continued collaborations with FFT, ETO-Watch etc, including co-convening of annual Thai forum on Business and Human Rights, which engages relevant government agencies;aswell as engaging with UN Special Procedures and forums such as the UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights; and holding government and private sector actors accountable to their commitments, given their commitments to UNGP.
We will contributetoIP3stated objectives and outcomes by: • Strengthening grassroots mobilisation and networks, including through technical and strategic support, and facilitating their direct access and engagement with key national and regional forums and actors. • Engagingnational, regional and international media[SS4.1][KK4.2][GL4.3][SS4.4] to amplify community and civil society voices, inform public debates and decision-making through regular briefings and media advisories, coordinating media coverage of key events,co-convene media trips to affected communities, and where requested act as a resource person for media trainings etc • Building evidence base to advocate for more inclusive water governance, including through community action research, co-production of knowledge • Broadening and diversifying networks, including engaging and coordinating with youth groups, women leaders, policy and technical experts, researchers within Mekong and Salween basins and beyond • Monitoring, engaging and advocating keyactorsandinstitutions, including but not limited to governments, developers, financiers and regional and institutional 1.5.2 Activities Below we outline top-level activities we will undertake under Pillars 1 and 2. Also see section below and Annex 2 R<(>&<)>R 2026 Annual Work Plan for more details on activities planned for November 2025 to December 2026.
Pillar 1: GEDSI and Feminist Influencing Activities under this pillar are organised around three of the four strategic actions under the Draft IP3GEDSI Strategic Framework, 2025-209 (September 2025), which recognises that advancing inclusive water governance needs to be centred on the lived experience, voices and participation of marginalised groups, particularly women and socially excluded communities. Note, wedo not include Strategic Action 3, as this proposal is not focused on climate adaptation planning
Strategic Action 1. Advanceleadership and representation of diverse women, Indigenous Peoples, People with Disabilities, and other marginalised groups in WRG and climate resilience, by: ● Collaborating with community leaders and networks in target areas to strengthen and hone their advocacy and negotiation skills (e.g. Indigenous Karen in the Salween (CMU), Kok-Khong Women’s Network in Northern Thailand(LRA)) ● Promoting meaningful participation in national and regional processes and forums and engagement with relevant actors e.g. MRC, ADB, Thai Parliamentary Committees etc – (R<(>&<)>R coordinating with partners, including with LRA and CESD, CMU) ●Amplifying marginalised groups lived experiences and voices through media and communications e.g. media trips, communication products, profiles etc (R<(>&<)>R lead, but will coordinate with LRA, CESD, CMU and others) ● Co-convening exchanges to promote learning and networking (CESD, CMU on local researcher network in the Salween)
Strategic Action 2. Inclusive policy frameworks, governance systems, and advocacy platforms are strengthened to ensure meaningful participation and influence of marginalised groups, through: ● Community action research and co-production of knowledge e.g. CESD, CMU building on experiences of People’s EIA, LRA supporting Thai Baan research focused on women’s knowledge and perspectives on river pollution in Kok-Mekong rivers ● Build onthe processand results of community action research to promote greater recognition of local knowledge (R<(>&<)>R, LRA and CESD, CMU) ● Targeted engagement and advocacy to create more inclusive spaces and dialogues convened by other organisations e.g.Mekong River Commission (R<(>&<)>R)
Strategic Action 4. Increasedawareness and advocacy efforts to challenge discriminatory social norms and power relations, through: ● Collaborating with diverse organisations and networks to strengthen collective and inclusive organising andadvocacy (LRA, CESD, CMU, and R<(>&<)>R) ● Raising critical concerns about discriminatory policies and institutionalized practices that prevent inclusive and meaningful participation of marginalised groups, calling for remedial steps to be proactively implemented (R<(>&<)>R)
Pillar 2: Inclusive Water Resource Governance and Climate Resilience
• Strengthen community organizers and networks at strategic sites in Mekong and Salween basins in Thailand including e.g. Chiang Mai, Mae Hong Son and Tak provinces inThailand, which would be impacted by Salween Water Diversion Project; North and Northeast Thailand, which are threatened by hydropower and mining (LRA and CESD, CMU for local level; and R<(>&<)>R for networking at sub-national, national and regional level) • Support local and coordinate with national and regional civil society networks activities and campaigns to protect Salween and Mekong rivers against major threats, such as large hydro, water diversion and mining projects. Support will include e.g. providing information and analysis of projects, related policies and impacts to inform and strengthen network campaigns and strategies; facilitating access to and engagement with relevant national and regional institutions and mechanisms including key targets identified under Section 1.2 above. (LRA and CESD, CMU for local level; and R<(>&<)>R for networking at sub-national, national and regional level) • Engage media (e.g. briefings for journalists, convening media events, op-eds etc) to ensure civil society and community perspectives are included in media coverage and help inform regional debates related to rivers and dams (R<(>&<)>R). • With ETO-Watch, monitor Thai out-bound investments that impact on rivers and rights of communities in the Mekong and Salweenbasins, drawingon commitments in Thailand’s 2nd National Action Plan (NAP) on Business and Human Rights (2023-2027) related to extraterritorial obligations for Thai investors; and engage and influence the 3rd NAP (R<(>&<)>R) • With Fair Finance Thailand,continue to monitor and engage Thai banks involved in hydropower to strengthen lending policies and practices and advocate to shift financing away from large-scale hydropower (R<(>&<)>R) • With regional networks, such as NGO Forum on ADB, monitor and engage IFIs such asADB and World Bank, on plans and policies that impact water and energy issues in the Mekong region (R<(>&<)>R) Research, analysis and communications • Support, commission or undertake research and analysis to build evidence base and elevate marginalisegroupsvoicesandperspectives. These include but are not limited to CESD-supported community action research related to Yuam-Salween Water Diversion in Omkoi district and transboundary water contamination in the Salween mainstream in Tha Ta Fang village; LRA-supported Tai Baan research in the Kok-Mekong rivers; Production of Mekong (2026) and Salween (2026) Situation updates, technical analysis of the impacts of Phou Ngoy dam, coordinated by R<(>&<)>R etc. • Regular media engagement including coordinating media trips on priorityproject, sites and issues, media advisories, media streaming of key events and actions etc. We plan on co-organsing twomedia trips per year to affected communities. • Produce communications that amplify voices of women, Indigenous Peoplesand other marginalised groups.

participating-org.narrative: Rivers and Rights Foundation is a legally registered foundation in Thailand. We operate in full compliance with Thai laws and regulations governing foundations in Thailand. Our registration ensures that we meet all legal requirements, including adherenceto tax regulations, labor laws, and other relevant statutory obligations. As part of our commitment to transparency and accountability, Rivers and Rights fulfills all necessary reporting and filing requirements with Thai regulatory authorities and donors.This includes maintaining proper financial records, submitting tax filings as required by the Revenue Department, and complying with any legal obligations related to employment, contracts, and operational activities in Thailand. Our organization upholdsthe highest standards of governance, ensuring that all activities align with Thai legal frameworks while supporting our mission and objectives.
